Photograph: @selecaoportugal/X Cristiano Ronaldo Portugal immortalise Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt in tribute to national legend 
 Original No 7 design preserved to honour player
 Career brought 146 goals and three major titles
 Joti Birdi Sat 14 Nov 2026 14.13 EST Last modified on Sat 14 Nov 2026 15.09 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Portugal have made a permanent change to the No 7 shirt to honour the legacy of Cristiano Ronaldo and ensure the number remains forever associated with their greatest footballing icon.
 Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him? Read more The former forward, whose career spanned 23 years and 246 caps in which he scored 146 goals, announced his retirement on 5 November after a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus. His last appearance for Portugal was on 24 September, in a 1-0 home win over Wales in the Nations League.
 Before their Nations League clash against Denmark, Portugal tweeted a unique design change to the iconic No 7 shirt to ensure Ronaldo’s version remains immortalised.
 The small change to the number 7 is an acknowledgement of the star’s playing career in which he broke the men’s all-time scoring record. He captained his country to their first major trophy at Euro 2016, before adding two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.
 Portugal will also pay tribute to Ronaldo before and during their Nations League fixture against Denmark in Braga on Saturday.
 View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo wore the iconic No 7 shirt for 20 years in a career that lasted 23 years for Portugal. Photograph: Armando França/AP “Time to debut a new 7. Because there’s one that will be eternal,” the Portuguese national team wrote on social media on Saturday. The post included a goat emoji to signify “Greatest Of All Time”.
